title: Setting Expense Categories and Budgets That Actually Work for a Small Team
summary: Learn how to structure realistic expense categories and flexible budget thresholds that keep small business spend organized without overwhelming your team.
author: The SnapSME Team

sections.heading: The Category Dilemma: Too Simple vs. Too Complex
content: Setting up expense categories for a small team is a delicate balance. If your categories are too broad (e.g. putting everything into 'General Expenses'), you lose visibility into where your money is actually going.

On the other hand, if your category list is overly complicated with 50 specific accounting codes, team members get confused and select categories at random. The goal is to establish 6 to 10 clear, intuitive categories that everyone understands immediately.

sections.heading: The Core 8 Expense Categories for Small Businesses
sections.content: Here is a proven, simplified category structure that works seamlessly for most small teams (2 to 10 employees):
bullets: Fuel & Transport: Gas, diesel, parking fees, tolls, public transit, and vehicle maintenance.
Office Supplies: Paper, stationery, ink cartridges, small desk accessories, and shipping fees.
Meals & Food: Client lunches, team meals, and overtime food for job sites.
Equipment & Tools: Hardware, job-site tools, safety gear, and minor office equipment.
Utilities & Bills: Electricity, internet, phone services, and facility costs.
Software & Subscriptions: Cloud software, domain renewals, design apps, and digital services.
Petty Cash Spend: Minor cash outlays and incidental job expenses.
Other Expenses: Miscellaneous business expenses that fall outside core categories.

sections.heading: Setting Realistic Budgets for Small Teams
content: Budgeting in a small business shouldn't be about rigid restrictions that slow down daily work. Instead, view budgets as guardrails that prevent unexpected cost overruns.

Start by reviewing 3 months of past spending data. Establish monthly target caps for major discretionary categories like Meals, Fuel, and Software. Review progress weekly so adjustments can be made before month-end.
sections.callout: Use category budgets as targets, not strict barriers. Give managers small discretionary thresholds so business operations stay agile.

sections.heading: Automating Category Mapping with Smart OCR
content: Modern expense software eliminates manual category selection entirely. When a team member snaps a receipt photo from a gas station or hardware store, intelligent OCR automatically suggests the correct category based on the merchant name.
This saves time, reduces human error, and keeps your accounting data clean and consistent month after month.
